headline: Amazon's Alexa Tablet 12 Pro launches with Nanomatte display and Google Play for $499
summary: Amazon's new premium tablet features a 12.3-inch Nanomatte display that virtually eliminates glare, full Google Play Store access, and starts at $499, aiming to compete with higher-end tablets.
details: Amazon has launched its new Alexa Tablet 12 Pro, a premium Android device starting at $499. This tablet aims to offer a high-end experience, featuring a 12.3-inch display with optional Nanomatte tech and full access to the Google Play Store.

The Nanomatte display is a standout feature, designed to almost completely eliminate glare, making the screen clearly readable even in bright sunlight. This coating also gives the screen a more paper-like feel, enhancing the viewing experience.

For readers, the tablet includes an immersive Kindle mode with three display options: Standard, Color, and Ink (grayscale). This mode also extends battery life from 16 hours to 20 hours by limiting background activities and reducing eye strain.

Under the hood, the Alexa Tablet 12 Pro is powered by a MediaTek Dimensity 8400 8-core CPU and comes with 8GB or 12GB of RAM. Its aluminum unibody design is light at 550 grams, offering a premium feel without being flimsy.

The tablet deeply integrates Alexa, with an 'Ask Alexa' bar and a Dynamic Tab for proactive suggestions based on user habits. Amazon emphasizes privacy, with features like On-Screen Intelligence being strictly opt-in and robust controls for data.

Optional accessories include the Alexa Tablet Pro Pen and Pro Keyboard, which attach magnetically. While the keyboard is serviceable for light use, its shallow keys and two-part design might not suit all-day typing.

headline: Spotify renews Joe Rogan deal for $250 million, expanding to other platforms
summary: Spotify has renewed its multi-year licensing agreement with Joe Rogan, valued at an estimated $250 million. The deal expands 'The Joe Rogan Experience' beyond Spotify to other podcast platforms.
details: Spotify has renewed its multi-year licensing agreement with Joe Rogan, whose podcast remains the number one show on the platform and globally. The Wall Street Journal reports the deal is valued at around $250 million, allowing new episodes of The Joe Rogan Experience to appear on Spotify and other platforms.

This renewal builds on the lucrative relationship that began with an exclusive streaming agreement in 2020. The company later allowed the show to be distributed to YouTube, Apple, and other podcasting platforms as part of its 2024 deal.

Despite past controversies surrounding Rogan's show, Spotify continues the partnership. The company states that JRE remains a 'defining show on Spotify, with a massive global audience and a format built around wide-ranging, long-form conversations'.
